searchText: I discovered there was the same key (at least one) that was running on `prysm/nethermind` and `teku/geth`. This explained what I discovered here: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1151915778308845648/1151986098780778586 I guess no slasher is running so no slashing occurred. Was it an intended setup? fortunately teku nodes are configured to store non-canonical blocks so I have the proof 🙂 but there ore other more recent instances where proposers were effectively different.. Dencun testing call in 1h: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/859 but there ore other more recent If I'm remembering correctly, the outcome of the call is to not allow empty accounts in the genesis alloc - mainnet has: ```json "5ed3f1ebe2ae6756b5d8dc19cad02c419aa5778b": { "balance": "0x0" }, ``` and ```json "00c40fe2095423509b9fd9b754323158af2310f3": { "balance": "0x0" }, ``` What do we do here? Maybe I'm misinterpreting what clients should do? I was implementing a check that just stops the node when loading the genesis, if it has an empty account tests should still remove the empty accounts from the genesis alloc ig ~~ah, maybe we should just check for an empty system account? instead of any account~~ nvm, it does seem like the outcome of the call was to disallow any empty account
